 FILE PHOTO — Secretary of the State Stephanie Thomas speaks to reporters about early voting in Connecticut’s ongoing primary elections Thursday, Aug. 6, 2026, in front of Hartford City Hall. She is joined, L to R in the background, by Hartford Town & City Clerk Eric Lusa, Hartford Democratic Registrar of Voters Giselle “Gigi” Feliciano, and Hartford Mayor Arunan Arulampalam. Credit: Jamil Ragland / CTNewsJunkie 
 Many early voters have taken notice of a seemingly new requirement to sign an affirmation before voting, according to Secretary of the State Stephanie Thomas’ office. Although the requirement is not new, she said the change in voting tabulators has caused some concern among early voters.
 The answer, Thomas said, is that Connecticut law requires everyone who votes early to sign an affirmation.
 “Previously, voters signed the affirmation on the outside of their early voting ballot envelopes,” Thomas’ office said in a statement. “This year, voters place their completed ballots directly into tabulators instead of envelopes, so the affirmation is signed separately.”
 Thomas said she could see where the confusion came from.
 “If you’ve voted on Election Day for 30 years and never had to sign anything like this, I understand why you’d have questions,” she said. “Depending on the municipality, voters may see the affirmation in a logbook or on a separate sheet. Either way, your signature is kept separate from your ballot, and the affirmation does not reveal how you voted.”
 Before early voting, the voter must sign an affirmation, in accordance with Connecticut General Statutes § 9-163aa(e) , as amended by Public Act 26-1 .
 AFFIRMATION: I, the undersigned, do hereby state, under penalty of false statement (perjury), that:
 1. I am the elector appearing in person to vote at an election or primary prior to the day of such election or primary.
 2. I am eligible to vote in the election or primary indicated for today.
 3. I have identified myself to the satisfaction of the registrars of voters.
 4. I have not voted in person or by absentee ballot and I will not vote otherwise than by this ballot at this election or primary.
 5. I have received an early voting ballot for the purpose of so voting.
 For official election information, visit MyVote.CT.gov .
